hints: Sort all suffixes of the string.
A suffix contributes all its prefixes, except those already shared with the preceding suffix.
Compute the suffix array and adjacent longest common prefixes.
analogy: Sorted suffixes put identical beginnings next to each other, so shared prefixes need to be counted only once.
example: For aba, the distinct substrings are a, b, ab, ba, aba: five.
algorithm: Construct the suffix array and LCP array. For each suffix of length len, add len minus its LCP with the preceding suffix; use zero for the first suffix.
correctness: All prefixes of a suffix are substrings. In suffix order, any prefix already seen is shared with the immediately preceding suffix, and exactly the LCP-length prefixes are duplicates. Thus each distinct substring is counted once.
complexity: For length n, O(n log n) time using a doubling suffix array and O(n) space.
